article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Purple Punch × Gelato 45
Breeder: The Cali Connection
THC Content: 24%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Peach, citrus, sweet cream, fruit, hash
Flowering Time (Indoor): 63–67 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid October
Indoor Yield: 200–260 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Bellini borrows its name from the peach-and-citrus cocktail, but the comparison works because the flower genuinely moves in that direction rather than simply wearing a fashionable dessert label. Fresh buds can release ripe peach, orange peel, soft citrus, and creamy sweetness before a quieter layer of hash and earth begins to appear underneath.

The Cali Connection created the cultivar by crossing Purple Punch with Gelato 45, combining the dark-fruit relaxation of one parent with the smooth, heavily resinous dessert qualities of the other. What emerges is a modern California hybrid built as much around aroma and resin as potency. The plants have a strong central structure, respond well to topping and lateral training, clone readily, and finish in a practical 63–67-day window. For consumers, the appeal lies in a similarly balanced experience: a pleasant mental lift develops first, followed by a smoother body calm that becomes progressively more noticeable without immediately flattening the session.
Genetics and Lineage

The official breeder pedigree is Purple Punch × Gelato 45. Purple Punch is traditionally associated with Larry OG and Granddaddy Purple , a combination that brings together several classic California traits. Larry OG contributes lemon, earth, pine, resin, and the physical depth of the broader OG family , while Granddaddy Purple supplies grape, berry, coloration, and a heavier indica-oriented finish. Purple Punch became especially popular because it could produce sweet fruit, dense flowers, strong visual appeal, and substantial relaxation without requiring an unusually long flowering period.

Gelato 45 comes from Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies . Sunset Sherbet contributes creamy fruit, sweetness, and a soft dessert profile, while Thin Mint brings dough, mint, spice, earth, and the dense trichome production associated with Cookies-family cannabis . The #45 phenotype became one of the better-known Gelato selections because it combines flavor intensity with solid structure and considerable resin. In Bellini, that parent appears to soften Purple Punch’s darker fruit character and redirect it toward peach, citrus, cream, and a silkier finish.

Although both parents belong to the modern California dessert era, their aromatic personalities are different enough to give the cross a distinct identity. Purple Punch contributes weight, color, and richer fruit, while Gelato 45 adds creaminess, resin, and a smoother citrus-dessert quality. The Cali Connection’s breeder description emphasizes strong structure, easy cloning, solid yields, and a particularly fragrant terpene profile, indicating that the project was selected for horticultural usefulness as well as flavor.
Effects and Experience

Bellini generally fits the middle ground between a bright social hybrid and a relaxing evening strain. The first part of the experience can feel mentally uplifting, with mood becoming lighter and ordinary entertainment more engaging. Music , conversation, movies, gaming, or low-pressure creative work can all pair naturally with this phase because the cerebral effect is noticeable without necessarily becoming sharp or restless. The Gelato side helps give the mental lift a smooth, almost leisurely quality rather than the faster pace associated with Haze-dominant marijuana.

As time passes, Purple Punch influence becomes more apparent. The body starts to loosen, muscles feel less tense, and the pace of the session becomes calmer without immediately turning into couch-lock. That gradual shift makes the cultivar useful across the late afternoon and evening, especially for consumers who want some mental engagement before deeper relaxation sets in. Smaller doses tend to preserve the brighter side, while larger servings allow the heavier body component to take a more dominant role.

Because the breeder does not publish a single standardized THC percentage, potency should be judged from the actual batch rather than a universal strain number. Strong examples can still be highly intoxicating, particularly when the flower has been grown under intense light and harvested at full maturity. Excessive consumption may produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, mental haze, or temporary anxiety. Waiting for the first dose to develop fully is a better approach than allowing the smooth flavor to encourage rapid overconsumption.
Medical Benefits

For medical cannabis consumers, Bellini may be most relevant when stress and physical tension appear at the same time. The early mental lift can make repetitive thoughts or low mood feel less dominant for some people, while the later body relaxation may reduce how prominently soreness or muscular tightness occupies attention. Unlike extremely sedating marijuana, the cultivar can leave a window of functionality before the heavier phase begins, making it potentially useful during the transition from active daytime hours into a quieter evening.

Higher doses may bring stronger appetite stimulation and drowsiness as the Purple Punch side becomes more obvious. Consumers who use weed primarily to relax at night may appreciate that progression, while those hoping to remain active will generally prefer smaller servings. Individual response remains important because high-THC cannabis can produce anxiety or cognitive fog in sensitive users even when a strain is broadly associated with calm.

The breeder describes Bellini as highly terpene expressive but does not provide one fixed laboratory terpene profile for the seed line. The peach, citrus, sweet hash, and creamy qualities indicate a complex aromatic mix that can shift from plant to plant. Rather than assuming specific terpene percentages, medical consumers should rely on testing from the actual flower whenever available. Cannabinoid strength, terpene composition, medications, tolerance, and dosage are all more useful than the cultivar name alone when cannabis is being used therapeutically.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Peach is the defining flavor, but it does not appear in isolation. Fresh citrus sharpens the fruit, giving the bouquet a lively quality that can resemble peach nectar mixed with orange zest. Underneath sits a smoother creamy note from the Gelato side, while sweet hash adds enough depth to keep the flower from smelling like uncomplicated fruit candy. The breeder describes the finish as silky, an appropriate way to characterize the way these flavors blend rather than arriving as separate, competing notes.

Purple Punch can introduce a darker fruit character beneath the peach, occasionally pushing the aroma toward grape or ripe berry. Gelato 45 contributes more cream, dough, and resin, so individual plants may range from bright citrus-peach expressions to richer dessert-oriented phenotypes. Breaking the buds apart generally exposes more hash, mild earth, and a faint herbal edge than is obvious from the unopened flower.

On the palate, citrus and peach tend to arrive first, followed by sweet cream and a deeper hash-like finish. Vaporization usually preserves the delicate fruit notes most clearly, while combustion places greater emphasis on resin, earth, and the heavier dessert qualities. A slow drying period followed by a controlled cure is particularly valuable because peach and citrus aromas are easy to lose if the flowers are exposed to too much heat or dried too rapidly.
Growing Information

Bellini was selected as a practical modern hybrid rather than a difficult connoisseur plant. The Cali Connection describes strong overall structure and specifically notes that the cultivar clones well, an important advantage for growers who discover a particularly expressive peach phenotype. Plants can be grown with a dominant central cola, but topping encourages more lateral development and produces a broader, fuller structure that makes better use of horizontal lighting space.

Low-stress training works well after topping because the side branches can be guided outward into an even canopy. A trellis can then keep those branches separated and support flowering sites as buds gain mass. Growers working with fewer plants may find this wider structure especially useful, while those using a higher plant count can allow more natural vertical development. The plant is considered manageable enough for newer growers, provided basic environmental control is maintained.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 63–67 days, placing Bellini around nine to nine and a half weeks. The breeder lists yields at roughly 200–260 grams per square meter. That production level is solid rather than extreme, and the greater attraction is the quality of the finished flower and resin. Lighting, plant density, root volume, vegetative time, irrigation, and canopy management will influence whether a garden lands near or above the breeder reference.

As flowering advances, resin and aroma become increasingly important. The Cali Connection specifically highlights Bellini’s extract potential, describing a high and unusual terpene expression capable of producing fragrant concentrates. Rosin, dry sift, and ice-water hash can preserve the peach-citrus profile particularly well when the right phenotype is selected. For extraction-focused growers, aroma intensity may be more valuable than simply choosing the plant with the greatest dry flower weight.

Environmental consistency matters most during the final weeks. Dense flowers benefit from continuous airflow and moderate late-bloom humidity, while overcrowded interior growth should be removed selectively rather than aggressively stripped. Stable irrigation and balanced nutrition are generally enough to support the plant’s solid structure. Pushing fertilizer strength beyond what the roots can use is unlikely to improve the qualities that make the cultivar valuable.

Outdoors, the 63–67-day flowering window generally places harvest around early to mid-October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates, although local photoperiod and latitude can shift maturity. Full sunlight and unrestricted root space can produce substantially larger plants than indoor gardens. Regions with relatively dry autumns provide the easiest finish, while growers in wetter climates should keep the canopy open and monitor dense flowers closely as harvest approaches.
FAQ
What strains make Bellini?

The Cali Connection created Bellini by crossing Purple Punch with Gelato 45. Purple Punch is commonly traced to Larry OG × Granddaddy Purple, while Gelato 45 comes from Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies.
Is Bellini indica or sativa?

Bellini is best described as a balanced hybrid. Its effects often begin with an uplifting, easygoing cerebral phase before a progressively more relaxing body sensation develops. The breeder does not assign a strict indica-to-sativa percentage.
What does Bellini taste like?

Peach and citrus are the signature flavors, followed by creamy sweetness, fruit, sweet hash, and mild earth. Some phenotypes may reveal additional grape or berry influence from Purple Punch, while Gelato 45 can make the finish smoother and more dessert-like.
How long does Bellini take to flower?
The Cali Connection lists an indoor flowering period of approximately 63–67 days. Outdoors, plants generally reach maturity around early to mid-October in favorable Northern Hemisphere climates.
How much does Bellini yield?

The breeder lists indoor production at approximately 200–260 grams per square meter. Outdoor yield is not standardized and depends on sunlight, root volume, plant size, training, climate, and the length of the vegetative season.
Final Thoughts on Bellini

Bellini is a good example of modern dessert cannabis working best when the parent strains contribute more than sweetness. Purple Punch supplies dark fruit, physical depth, and colorful California genetics, while Gelato 45 adds cream, resin, structure, and the polished flavor that made Gelato such an influential breeding family. The peach-and-citrus expression gives the offspring a recognizable identity of its own.

Its experience follows a similarly balanced path. The mental opening is light enough for conversation, music, or entertainment, while the physical side gradually develops into a calmer and more settled state. Dose determines whether the strain remains comfortably functional or moves farther toward evening relaxation.

Cultivators get a manageable plant with strong structure, good cloning ability, and a 63–67-day bloom. Topping and lateral training can create a full canopy, while the breeder-listed 200–260 g/m² indoor yield provides respectable production. More important, the resin carries a high level of aromatic intensity that can translate particularly well into solventless extracts.

For growers and consumers interested in fruit-forward California hybrids, Bellini offers a profile that goes beyond generic berry sweetness. Peach, citrus, cream, hash, and a silky finish create a flavor that actually supports the cocktail-inspired name. Combined with a balanced effect and practical garden performance, that distinctive terpene character is what gives Bellini its place in our strain library .
